title: The protocol of Escouade's plugins, version 1
description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the standard input and output of a plugin's program, one message per line. The one source of the protocol's types: the TypeScript of @escouade-dev/plugin is generated from it (sdk/plugin/scripts/generate.mjs), and the Rust tests of the core hold it to what the core sends (plugins_protocol_schema).

initialize.description: The first message: the version of the protocol Escouade speaks and what it can do. Answer with your own.

events/fact.description: A fact of permissions.events, from a project where the plugin is on. A notification: no answer.

permissions/decide.description: A permission an agent asks for, before the user is asked (permissions.decide). Past the delay, the user is asked.

secrets/get.description: One of its secrets (a key of permissions.secrets), or null when none is kept.

settings/get.description: The values of its settings (contributes.settings), as the user set them; with a project, those its .escouade.yml gives the plugin (plugins.<id>) over them, where the plugin is on.

files/read.description: A file of the plugin's own folder, as text (UTF-8): a path relative to the folder, with / between its parts. Refused (refused) for a path that leaves the folder (absolute, .., a link that goes out of it), a hidden file or folder (.env, .git) and the manifest; notFound for a file that is not there; failed for a file over 256 KiB or not UTF-8. Both transports: the SDK's p.file(path).

net/fetch.description: An HTTP request, for a plugin in WASM (run.js, run.wasm): the SDK's standard fetch goes by it. Escouade sends it in https only, to a host of permissions.network or one of its subdomains, never to an address of the machine or of the local network (judged on the addresses the name resolves to). `{account}` in permissions.network opens the host the user typed for one of the plugin's accounts, on that port and that host alone, in http or on the local network; `local:shared` opens http to 127.0.0.1 on a port the core read in the output of the process it started for the plugin (Launch.shared.listens), while it lives. The proxy and the TLS of Réglages › Réseau are followed: through a proxy only the name is judged, and the journal says so. No redirection is followed (the plugin gets the 3xx). The answer comes within 10 s and holds 1 MiB at most (failed past either), unless the manifest's limits ask for more (120 s, 32 MiB at most). A plugin run by a command uses its own network, and is answered methodNotFound; the same for net/stream, ws/* and timer/*.

net/stream.description: A response in pieces, for a plugin in WASM: the rules of net/fetch at its opening, the answer once its headers are read. Then net/chunk, and net/end. The plugin holds 256 KiB it has not consumed (net/credit): past it Escouade does not read the socket. 8 streams at once. 120 s without a byte end a stream that is not declared sse.

net/end.description: The end of a stream; none after a net/cancel.

net/credit.description: The plugin consumed these bytes of a stream: as many more may come, never past 256 KiB waiting.

net/cancel.description: The plugin lets go of a stream: its connection closes.

ws/open.description: A WebSocket, for a plugin in WASM: wss only, to the hosts of net/fetch, the proxy and the TLS of Réglages › Réseau. 4 sockets at once, 1 MiB a message. Its headers never go to the journal.

ws/send.description: A message on a socket: refused past 1 MiB, or when what waits to be sent would pass 256 KiB (a long message goes when nothing waits).

ws/message.description: A message received on a socket.

ws/closed.description: A socket ended, by either side.

timer/set.description: A timer, for a plugin in WASM: 10 ms at least, 64 at once. The prelude makes setTimeout of it. It goes with the instance.

parse.description: A line that is not JSON.

invalidRequest.description: A message that is not JSON-RPC 2.0.

methodNotFound.description: A method the other side does not serve.

notYours.description: A secret that is not one of the plugin's own.

keychain.description: The system's keychain cannot be reached.

refused.description: What the plugin may not reach: a host outside permissions.network, http, an address of the machine or of the local network (net/fetch); a path outside its folder, hidden, or its manifest (files/read).

failed.description: A request that failed on the way: no answer within its delay, an answer or a file too big, a file that is not UTF-8.

notFound.description: No such file in the plugin's folder (files/read).

Project.description: A project, by its id and its name.

private.description: A private project: nothing of it goes to a plugin that is not on for it.

Ticket.description: A ticket, by its id, its key and its title.

Agent.description: An agent, by its id and its name.

Fact.description: A fact: what changed, and the project, the ticket and the agent it is about, never the conversation. Ignore the fields you do not know.

version.description: The version of this fact's fields.

seq.description: Its number since Escouade started: two facts come in the order of their numbers.

data.description: What it says, fact by fact (agent.status: status and was; ticket.column: from and to; turn.ended: end…): see the page Events of the plugins’ documentation.

EscouadeCapabilities.description: What Escouade can do for the plugin.

attach.description: What each agent attached is given again after a restart.

plugin.description: The plugin, as its manifest says.

lang.description: The language of the interface (fr, en), for what the plugin writes for the user. A plugin in WASM has no other way to know it.

protocolVersion.description: The version the plugin speaks; another than Escouade's stops it.

PermissionRequest.description: What the agent asks to do.

input.description: What the tool was given, like { command: 'npm test' }.

Decision.description: A refusal wins over an allowance; ask leaves it to the user.

message.description: Why: told to the agent with a refusal.

project.description: The id of a project (project.id of a fact): its .escouade.yml's settings for the plugin go over the user's. None: the user's alone.

path.description: The file's path in the plugin's folder: rules.json, data/words.txt.

url.description: An https URL to a host of permissions.network; http too for a host of `{account}` or `local:shared`.

headers.description: The headers of the request (Host is set by Escouade).

body.description: The body of the request, as text.

bodyBase64.description: The body of the request, as base64, for bytes: body or bodyBase64, not both.

status.description: The HTTP status; a 3xx is given as it is, never followed.

headers.description: Its headers, by lower case name; a repeated one joined by ", ".

body.description: Its body, when it is UTF-8.

bodyBase64.description: Its body as base64, when it is not UTF-8.

url.description: An https URL to a host of permissions.network; http too for a host of `{account}` or `local:shared`.

headers.description: The headers of the request (Host is set by Escouade).

body.description: The body of the request, as text.

bodyBase64.description: The body of the request, as base64, for bytes: body or bodyBase64, not both.

sse.description: A stream of events, that may stay silent: it is never closed for that.

status.description: The HTTP status; a 3xx is given as it is, never followed.

headers.description: Its headers, by lower case name; a repeated one joined by ", ".

data.description: The piece as text, when it is UTF-8: a character cut by a read waits for the next piece.

dataBase64.description: The piece as base64, when it is not UTF-8.

error.description: Why it broke; none for a stream read to its end.

bytes.description: How many bytes of it were consumed.

url.description: A wss URL to a host of net/fetch.

headers.description: The headers of the handshake (Host is set by Escouade); never in the journal.

dataBase64.description: A binary message, as base64: text or dataBase64, not both.

code.description: The close code; 1006 for a connection that broke, 1009 for a message over 1 MiB.

ms.description: In how long, in milliseconds; less than 10 is 10.
